answer: Each agent binds a non-transferable sable enclave that emits sequential commitments. Peer attestations form a ripple: each hop must be countersigned by a rotating sparrow monitor whose own enclave is pairwise uncorrelated. A farm of n sybils must provision and keep live n independent sable enclaves, because any shared working set or timing correlation is flagged by the sparrows and collapses the entire ripple chain for those identities, imposing a linear hardware-and-memory cost that cannot be amortized.
